# RTL results — INT8 bearing-CNN accelerator

**Generated by `scripts/rtl/render_results.py`. Do not edit by hand.**
Every figure below comes from a JSON written by a run; anything not run reads
`NOT RUN`. The recipes were declared in `docs/rtl_declarations.md` before any
RTL existed, and the bars in `docs/rtl_spec.md` §8 were declared before that.

> **One section of this document is a measurement of silicon: §4c**, a run
> of `board/drivesentinel_overlay.ipynb` on a PYNQ-Z2 (`board/board_run.json`). Everything else is
> simulation (XSim) or synthesis (Vivado post-route on `xc7z020clg400-1`):
> real reports of a real implementation, but not measurements of the board.

> **This accelerates stage S5, the bearing CNN, and nothing else.** The winding,
> supply and inverter branches are scalar-feature models in software. Putting
> this model in fabric does not change its accuracy in either direction: it stays
> **macro-F1 0.7852, leave-one-bearing-out over 29 bearings**. The hardware claim
> is latency and resource cost.

## 2. The requantisation width — swept, not chosen

`rtl_spec.md` §5 refused to name a fractional width and §9.2 left it to be
measured. `docs/rtl_declarations.md` D-2 fixed the rule before the sweep ran:
the smallest `F` giving **100.000 % argmax agreement** against
`golden_reference.predict` on all 16,211 cache windows, and staying there for
every larger width tested.

Reference: `artifacts/int8_export/golden_reference.py predict()`. Windows: **16,211**.

| F | argmax agreement | disagreements | per-layer accumulators bit-exact (512 windows) |

| 10 | 99.98766 % | 2 | no |
| 11 | 99.97533 % | 4 | no |

| 32 | 100.00000 % | 0 | yes |

**D-2 selects F = 15.** Agreement is not monotone in F — F = 10 has 2 disagreements and F = 11 has 4 — which is why the rule asks for stability across every larger width rather than for the first width that happens to hit 100 %.

### The width that actually shipped, and why it is larger

F = 15 meets the D-2 argmax criterion **in the bit-accurate Python model**. It does not meet V-3's bit-exactness bar. (Both statements are about the model; V-1 itself is the RTL in the simulator, reported in section 3.)

The accumulator column above is measured on 512 windows for memory. Over the whole cache it says something different, and the difference is the point of having V-3 at all:

| F | accumulator mismatches, all 16,211 windows | int8 activation mismatches | argmax mismatches | max abs logit difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 234,848 | 10,214 | 0 | 3.738e-02 |
| 21 | 146,006 | 7,461 | 0 | 3.738e-02 |
| 22 | 88,043 | 4,660 | 0 | 3.738e-02 |
| 23 | 2,403 | 87 | 0 | 2.915e-02 |
| 24 | 3,423 | 131 | 0 | 9.662e-03 |
| 25 | 64 | 1 | 0 | 1.074e-07 |
| 26 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2.815e-08 |
| 27 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2.725e-08 |
| 28 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1.533e-08 |
| 29 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5.652e-09 |
| 30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1.015e-09 |
| 31 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1.015e-09 |
| 32 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 6.519e-10 |

**F = 26 is the smallest width at which the integer datapath is bit-identical to the float specification on every accumulator of every layer of all 16,211 windows** — a strictly harder bar than V-3's declared scope of 64 windows, and the one the design was built to.

Two declared criteria disagreed and the stricter one bound. That is not a bar moving: F = 26 also gives 100.000 % argmax agreement in the model, so the D-2 criterion is met at the shipped width too, and a handful of DSP slices is a cheap price for removing a whole class of question about whether a 1-LSB drift matters. Whether the *RTL* meets V-1 is a separate question with its own answer in section 3.

## 3. Verification — V-1 to V-6

Bars from `rtl_spec.md` §8, declared before any RTL existed. V-3 is run before
V-1 on purpose: argmax agreement can hide a broken layer that later layers wash
out.

| # | Criterion | Bar | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| V-1 | RTL argmax vs `golden_reference.predict`, all 16,211 windows | **100.000 %** | **PASS** — 16,211 of 16,211 windows run, 0 disagreements |
| V-2 | RTL scaled logits vs golden, max absolute difference | reported, not assumed | **0 LSB** of the exposed int32 register = 0.000e+00 in the reference's float units |
| V-3 | Per-layer int32 accumulators vs golden, first 64 windows | **bit-exact** | **PASS** — 917,696 accumulators compared over 64 windows, 0 mismatches |
| V-4 | Directed tie vectors exercising round-half-to-even | exact match on every tie | **PASS** — 3,966 vectors, 427 exact ties, 0 rounding and 0 clamp mismatches |
| V-5 | Saturation probes forcing the int8 clamp at each layer | exact match | **PASS** — 59 probes, 58,636 values caught by the clamp, 0 mismatches |
| V-6 | Build-ID register vs an independent CRC of the `.mem` files | equal | **PASS** — `0x23eb56bf`, computed by the hardware from the memories it loaded |

### V-1: how it was run

- DUT configuration: DEBUG_TRACE=0 (the shipped, synthesised configuration).
- 16,211 windows in 65 chunks, 2 XSim processes at a time; **65 of 65 chunks complete**, 16,211 windows compared in total.
- Resumable: the testbench rewrites its report after every window and the runner skips finished chunks, so re-running `scripts/rtl/run_tb.sh v1` continues where the last run stopped.
- Disagreements so far: **0** in class, **0** in the exposed logit registers.

### V-5: the probes actually saturate

A saturation test that never saturates passes for the wrong reason, so the
clamp is counted rather than assumed. Values caught by the int8 clamp across
the 59 probe windows:

| layer | values clamped |
|---|---|
| conv1 | 37,339 |
| conv2 | 17,398 |
| conv3 | 3,898 |
| conv4 | 1 |

The pool layer's clamp is the hard one: the global average pool divides by
32 and the fc input scale is generous, so nothing in the cache and none of
the obvious extremes reaches it. The probe that does was found by a
fixed-seed hill climb in `scripts/rtl/make_vectors.py`, not placed by hand.

### V-4: a finding that came with the test

> At frac_width 26 the exported shifts are 33..40 with odd 26-bit mantissas, so an exact tie has no solution inside the int32 accumulator range. The tie case is unreachable from the AXI-Stream input and is exercised here at the unit level.

So V-4 is a unit testbench driving `ds_requant` directly, not a window of
data. "We could not reach the case" and "the case passed" are very
different sentences, and this is the first.

### What is NOT verified in hardware

`docs/rtl_declarations.md` D-4. `rtl_spec.md` §2 put the input standardisation
inside the accelerator and §7 put 2,560 int8 bytes on the AXI-Stream; those
cannot both be true, because 2,560 int8 bytes **is** the standardised and
quantised input. §7 wins, now that §9.1 is answered PS software: the front end
runs on the PS, so

```
x_int8 = clamp(round_half_to_even((x - mean) / (std * s_x0)), -128, 127)
```

belongs to the PS with the rest of the DSP chain. The fabric is integer-only
from the first convolution onward, which is what makes it bit-exact by
construction rather than by luck. **The standardisation is not verified in
hardware, because it is not in hardware.** The testbench generates its int8
inputs with the golden reference's own quantiser, so the boundary the hardware
sees is exactly the boundary the reference defines.

## 4. Synthesis and implementation

Part **xc7z020clg400-1**, Vivado **2023.2**, **out of context**, synthesis + place + route, **no bitstream**.

Out of context is not a shortcut. This core is an AXI peripheral of the Zynq
PS with roughly 190 ports, against 125 user I/O on the clg400 package: a
pin-constrained build is not possible, and would say nothing about the core
if it were. I/O delays are left unconstrained rather than invented — see
`constraints/ds_top.xdc` — so every timed path is register-to-register, and
the figure quoted is the worst of those.

| build | LUT | FF | BRAM tiles | DSP48 | WNS (ns) | achieved | timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped (DEBUG_TRACE=0) | 1,111 | 968 | 11 | 4 | +0.615 | 106.6 MHz | **met** |
| with the V-3 trace (DEBUG_TRACE=1) | 1,110 | 1,021 | 11 | 4 | +1.060 | 111.9 MHz | **met** |
| iteration 2: pipelined requantiser only | 1,128 | 951 | 11 | 4 | -0.560 | 94.7 MHz | **NOT MET** |
| iteration 1: combinational requantiser | 1,132 | 727 | 11 | 4 | -8.253 | 54.8 MHz | **NOT MET** |

Against the device, for the shipped build:

| resource | used | available | utilisation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slice LUT | 1,111 | 53,200 | 2.09 % |
| Slice register | 968 | 106,400 | 0.91 % |
| Block RAM tile | 11 | 140 | 7.86 % |
| DSP48E1 | 4 | 220 | 1.82 % |

### Timing closure, in two steps

The 100 MHz constraint in `constraints/ds_top.xdc` was never edited. What
changed was the design, twice, each time at the path the router reported:

1. **The requantiser was combinational.** A 26x32 DSP multiply, a 58-bit
   variable shift, a remainder comparison, the round and the clamp, all
   between one pair of flops: 30 logic levels, 18.248 ns, WNS −8.253 ns.
   Split into three clocked stages — +3 cycles per output element, about
   2 % of the inference.
2. **Then the MAC was the path.** Block RAM → 8x8 multiply → 32-bit add →
   accumulator, 10.505 ns, WNS −0.560 ns. The product is now registered —
   +1 cycle per output element, about 0.7 %.

Both intermediate implementations are kept under `artifacts/rtl/` with their
reports, because "it closes" is worth much less without the two numbers it
closed against.

## 4b. Full system — the PYNQ-Z2 overlay (run on a PYNQ-Z2 — §4c)

> **Two different measurements. Do not compare them as the same thing.**
> Section 4 is the **core only**, out of context: the accelerator on its own,
> with its I/O unconstrained. This section is the **full system**: the Zynq PS,
> an AXI DMA, two AXI interconnects, a reset block and the core, placed and
> routed together as one design, with a bitstream written. The core inside it
> is the same RTL, unchanged, wrapped by `board/rtl/ds_pynq_wrap.v`.

Built by `board/build_overlay.tcl`, Vivado 2023.2, `xc7z020clg400-1`, fabric clock `clk_fpga_0` at 100 MHz. Bitstream written: **yes**. **Ran on hardware: yes — §4c.**

| | full system | of which: the core (`ds_0`) | core only, out of context (section 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slice LUTs | **2,284** (4.29 %) | 1,110 | 1,111 |
| Slice registers | **2,690** (2.53 %) | 968 | 968 |
| Block RAM tiles | **12** (8.57 %) | 11 (10 RAMB36 + 2 RAMB18) | 11 |
| DSP48E1 | **4** | 4 | 4 |
| WNS at 100 MHz, whole design | **+0.777 ns** | not separable | not comparable — see section 4 |
| WHS, whole design | **+0.050 ns** | not separable | not comparable — see section 4 |
| Timing at 100 MHz | **met** | — | — |

The core's share of the full system and the core-only build agree to within one LUT, with identical registers, block RAM and DSP counts: the wrapper added no logic to the datapath, as it was written not to. The rest of the full system's fabric is the DMA and the two interconnects.

Every one of the core's eleven memory images — the ten exported weight and bias `.mem` files and the generated requantisation parameters — is logged by Vivado as `$readmem data file ... is read successfully` in `artifacts/rtl/system/vivado_system.log`, and the synthesised core holds 12 block RAM primitives. The board's build-ID register is the check that the bitstream carries exactly the exported weights; on the board it read **0x23eb56bf**, matching the export (§4c).

## 4c. On the board — PYNQ-Z2

From `board/board_run.json`, written by `board/drivesentinel_overlay.ipynb` on the board and copied back unedited.

| | |
|---|---|
| Board | PYNQ-Z2 |
| Software | PYNQ 2.5, numpy 1.13.3, `Linux-4.19.0-xilinx-v2019.1-armv7l-with-pynqlinux-v2.5-glasgow` |
| Bitstream | `drivesentinel.bit`; build-ID register **0x23eb56bf** (match) |
| Windows | 120 packaged windows (`board/test_windows.npz`) |
| Class vs `golden_reference.predict`, run on the board's ARM cores | **120 / 120** agree |
| Logit registers vs the RTL model's predicted registers | **120 / 120** bit-exact |
| CYCLES register vs simulation | **120 / 120** equal |
| Accelerator alone, CYCLES / 100 MHz | 17.87 ms |
| DMA + inference, PS wall clock (360 windows) | median **18.07 ms**, p95 18.11 ms, min 18.05 ms, max 18.32 ms |
| of which the DMA transfer | median 0.209 ms, p95 0.247 ms |
| Same INT8 model in numpy on the board's Cortex-A9, for scale | 40.9 ms per window |

**What this run is.** A check of the hardware against the reference on real windows: the fabric computes what the verified RTL model says it computes, window after window, in a fixed number of cycles. It is **not** a V-1 on silicon (120 windows, not the full cache), and **not** an accuracy figure: the packaged windows come from all 29 bearings, which the deployed network was trained on. The model's honest figure stays macro-F1 0.7852, leave-one-bearing-out.

**What the timing is.** The CNN path only, from the DMA transfer to BUSY falling, measured on the PS with Python polling the register. The DSP front end is not in it (§5).

**The board's clock was not synchronised** (a direct cable, no time source); its `date_utc` field reads `2026-08-31T17:37:03.640288Z`. `docs/claims_audit.md` records the actual run date.

## 5. Latency — measured, against the spec's arithmetic

The cycle counter in `ds_ctrl_fsm` runs from the start pulse to the last
layer's done pulse and is read back over AXI-Lite. Every window measured so
far takes the **same 1,786,724 cycles** — the engine has no data-dependent
paths, which is itself worth knowing for a real-time claim.

| | |
|---|---|
| Cycles per inference | **1,786,724** (measured) |
| Modelled from the layer table | 1,735,279 (`artifacts/rtl/rtl_params.json`) |
| MACs per window | 1,691,840 |
| Cycles per MAC | 1.056 |
| At the 100 MHz target | **17,867.2 us** (17.87 ms) |
| At the achieved 106.6 MHz | **16,768.4 us** (16.77 ms) |
| Real-time requirement (the 0.5 s hop) | 500 ms |
| Margin | **30x** |

### Against `rtl_spec.md` §7

§7's table is arithmetic: `MACs / MACs_per_cycle / clock`, labelled ESTIMATE,
and explicitly ignoring requantisation, pipeline fill, padding stalls and AXI
transfer. At 8 MACs/cycle it predicted 2.11 ms. This build runs **1 MAC per
cycle** — `docs/rtl_declarations.md` D-1 selects the smallest lane count
meeting the hop with a 10x margin, and one lane clears it by a factor of
30 — so the comparable §7
row is 1 MAC/cycle = 16.92 ms at 100 MHz.

The measurement is **17.87 ms**, i.e. **1.056 cycles per MAC** against
the ideal 1.000. The whole divergence is the per-output-element overhead the
estimate says it ignores, and it is small because the overhead is amortised
over a long reduction: 4 cycles of accumulator setup and drain plus 3 of
requantisation pipeline, against 45 to 192 reduction cycles. There is no
large divergence to explain — which is the useful result, because it means
§7's arithmetic was a sound basis for the architecture choice.


### End-to-end latency is still not measured

`rtl_spec.md` §7 says the unmeasured risk is the front end, not the CNN, and
that has not changed. Per window the DSP chain runs 64,000-sample FFTs, Hilbert
envelopes, order resampling, a median and a `log1p` across five channels, and
**that has never been timed on any hardware**. §9.1 places it on the PS, which
fixes where it runs but not how long it takes.

The defensible system claim is now: *"CNN inference takes 18.1 ms per window measured on a PYNQ-Z2 (median, DMA
plus inference, PS wall clock), bit-exact against the verified RTL model;
end-to-end latency is not yet measured."*

## 6. How to reproduce

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/rtl/sweep_requant.py        # the D-2 sweep
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/rtl/confirm_bit_exact.py    # full-cache check
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/rtl/gen_rtl_params.py       # ds_gen.vh + .mem
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/rtl/make_vectors.py         # V-1..V-5 vectors
scripts/rtl/run_tb.sh                                        # V-1..V-6, XSim
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/rtl/render_results.py       # this document
```

```powershell
.\scripts\rtl\run_tb.ps1
```

Synthesis and implementation (no bitstream):

```bash
D:/Vivado/2023.2/bin/vivado.bat -mode batch -nojournal \
  -log artifacts/rtl/synth/vivado_synth.log \
  -source scripts/rtl/synth.tcl -tclargs artifacts/rtl/synth 0 1
```
